notes: This is a decision-tree economic model: the model is recorded as an 'other' procedure and 3% discounting as a transformation, while benefit-cost ratios and net savings are arithmetic on model outputs. Influenza, COVID-19 and RSV vaccines are excluded from the model, so results are modelled rather than observed. No interval or test is reported, so inference is none.
view_issues: The Discussion calls $2.9 trillion 'societal savings' and '$11' per $1, but $2.9 trillion is gross benefit; net societal savings are $2.7 trillion (Results, Table 2). Table 1 gives diphtheria illnesses and hospitalizations both as 7,528, which may be a transcription error.
